newsitem.title: UK: HSBC's Bond would like asset manager buy.
newsitem.headline: HSBC's Bond would like asset manager buy.

text.p: Banking and financial giant HSBC Holdings will buy an asset management company to increase its capacity in the area if it can find something at the right price, its chief executive John Bond said on Wednesday.
Bond told Reuters in an interview that asset management was the only investment banking activity which HSBC was looking to expand by acquisition.
"The only area where you could expect us to make a purchase if we could find the right property is in asset management," Bond said.
He added that there are relatively few properties available and then the question of the price has to be overcome.

Bond was specific about the kind of company that HSBC would be looking at given that the bank has long standing fund management expertise in its Asia-Pacific heartland, expertise in the UK but a relatively small amount of funds under management in the United States.

"Our preference would be for retail," he said. "So it is an American purchase with ideally a retail client base that wants to have an overseas investment capability and that has hitherto been domestic. That's the kind of profile we would look for."
Asked if HSBC is actively looking for such a buy, Bond answered that the bank gets shown a huge number of investment opportunities although he added that 99 percent of them are quickly passed by.
Bond reiterated HSBC's position that it wants to continue strong control of the volatility of its earnings stream and that part of investment banking earnings are inherently volatile.

HSBC has two guidelines -- it will not allow dealing profits to be more than 10 percent of its revenues, and that it "would pause for thought if investment banking profits exceeded 12 percent of our net income."
The chief executive noted that currently the percentage stands at around five percent and concluded there was room for further growth before consideration would have to be given.
Another area of potential growth, among many in which HSBC is involved, is HSBC's UK unit Midland Bank, which was one of the star performers in the group's half-year results earlier this week.
Bond said Midland is likely to be built organically with improved productivity and by selling more products to customers.
"We think it's well within Midland's capability to sell more insurance and more unit trusts," Bond said. "We would like to see perhaps three products per customer."
He declined to be specific on where Midland stood in this aim now but said there was still room for improvement.
Bond said it was very hard "to make the numbers work" with acquisitions in the UK, adding that the only reason to make an acquisition would be to add to an existing client base.
"You don't have to buy another company to be able to produce products, you don't have to buy a life assurance company in order to write a life assurance policy," Bond said.
He added that HSBC sees the convergence in the UK financial services industry as meaning the need to gain new clients.
"But we have nothing on the agenda today, we are value conscious and we believe that the market attaches greater value to revenue growth than it does to cost cutting...although you have to do both."
Bond said revenue growth can be generated organically with Midland, providing value for shareholders.
